answer: Split attestations into orchard rows: each identity sits in one row, and any quorum must include members from two rows, so a clone farm confined to one branch can never certify itself. Weight is min-cut bounded across rows: splitting stake across n sybils drops each clone to 1/n influence, not n flat tolls. Joining costs one copper receipt per verified enclave, non-transferable and expiring, so a thousand identities need a thousand real devices. The group posts a ferrous bond that rusts when a correlated audit failure fires, so sacrificing one clone costs everyone's collateral.
